summary: Browser visual-regression tool pack, deliberately holding the two halves of the job that are stdlib and deterministic — it never drives a browser, because Playwright needs pip plus a ~150 MB download and a screenshot is non-deterministic by default. playwright-scaffold.py emits a determinism-hardened Playwright harness into the caller's own repo (fixed viewport per breakpoint, deviceScaleFactor 1, reduced motion, UTC, en-US, pinned colour scheme, frozen clock, font-hinting off, animation-kill CSS, networkidle plus an explicit settle assertion, and with --ci github a workflow pinning the Playwright container image, the only way font rasterisation stays stable across runners), refusing to overwrite without --force. png-diff.py compares two PNGs with a hand-rolled zlib+struct codec and fails on either of two gates: changed-pixel ratio, which catches drift, and largest 4-connected cluster, which catches a small structural shift that a ratio hides — and it refuses 16-bit, palette and interlaced input rather than guessing a green verdict over pixels it never read.
